historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-path 10-year attributable revenue CAGR after mid-cycle normalisation (FY0 at peak prices -> $10,000/t copper mid-cycle, plus Khoemacau expansion volumes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs (22.8% 3yr, 33.4% 5yr) are inflated by the June 2024 rights issue, the Oct-2025/Jun-2026 convertibles' equity components and the June 2026 US$797.6m placing - they are not organic. EPS 5yr is undefined (FY2020 EPS negative). Revenue and FCF CAGRs are cycle-position artefacts: FY2022 FCF (249.8 owner basis) was a blockade/price trough, so the 85% 3yr FCF CAGR is meaningless. None of the historical CAGRs is a usable forward rate for a miner valued off a commodity deck; the forward rate is set by the price deck and the volume pipeline.

scenario_narratives.base: MMG is a leveraged bet on one asset and one metal: Las Bambas is ~72% of revenue and ~80% of EBITDA, and copper is ~70% of revenue. The base case assumes the cycle normalises rather than persists - copper from a $13,000-14,600/t peak back to a $10,000/t mid-cycle over two years, with precious-metal by-product credits normalising alongside - while volumes grow modestly (FY2026 guidance up to 528kt copper) and the Khoemacau expansion adds ~70kt consolidated (38kt attributable) from H1-2028. Mid-cycle attributable EBITDA margin 50%, capex stepping down from the guided US$1.6-1.7bn once the Botswana expansion is built, cash tax 33% on EBIT. The convertibles are debt; the count is flat. The result is a mid-cycle value that sits near today's price: the market is pricing roughly a mid-cycle deck, not spot.
scenario_narratives.bull: The copper deficit thesis (electrification, grid and data-centre demand, no new mine supply) keeps the price at $12,000/t+ rather than $10,000/t, and MMG executes: Las Bambas at the top of guidance with no corridor stoppages, Khoemacau to 130kt on time and phase 2 sanctioned, by-product credits sustained by elevated gold and silver. Margins hold at the current 55%, capex intensity falls post-expansion, and the balance sheet (6% gearing after the placing and convertibles) funds a further acquisition without dilution. This is the scenario in which both convertibles convert; on an if-converted basis the per-share value is ~2.3% below the figure shown (HK$13.34).
scenario_narratives.bear: Price normalisation overshoots to $8,500/t copper on a demand slowdown just as a Las Bambas corridor blockade year lands (Peru's 2026 election, the August 2026 fatal accident investigation, illegal-mining encroachment at Sulfobamba), so Y2-Y3 revenue falls ~23% and attributable margins drop to 42%. The Khoemacau expansion runs late and over budget, Peru tightens the mining tax regime, and the Nickel Brazil deal - if it closes - puts US$350m into an oversupplied ferronickel market. Governance remains a discount: 63.7% Minmetals ownership, life-of-mine related-party offtake, and the shareholder loans that were refinanced in July 2026. Bear value is roughly two-thirds of today's price; the stock is not priced for this path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical miner is valued on a mid-cycle commodity deck, not on trailing peak earnings. FY0 is the TTM to June 2026 at H1-2026's $13,088/t copper, and the model's first job is to take that down to a $10,000/t base deck before capitalising anything - a 12x terminal cap on a finite-life asset base, 33% cash tax, and the full guided capex program. Flows are attributable (37.5%/45% JV partners stripped at the component level), the US$1.3bn of zero-coupon convertibles are debt at face, the count is flat, and jurisdiction risk sits in a 9.5% USD WACC while cycle and operational risk sit in a 30/50/20 scenario weighting. House and street values coincide because SBC is nil.
key_risks_to_valuation: Copper price deck: every $1,000/t on copper is roughly US$290m of attributable revenue (~5%) at near-full margin; the gap between spot ($14,600/t) and the base mid-cycle ($10,000/t) is the whole bull/base spread
Las Bambas corridor blockades, illegal mining and the August 2026 fatal-accident investigation - a lost quarter at Las Bambas is ~US$500m of attributable EBITDA
Peru political/tax regime (2026 election cycle) - the 33% cash tax rate assumes no new royalty or windfall tax
Khoemacau expansion execution: US$400m/yr of attributable-55% capex for a 2028 first-production date; delay or overrun hits years 4-5 of the base path
Convertible treatment: at values above ~HK$9.47 the if-converted basis is the lower one; the bull case is ~2.3% overstated on that basis (HK$13.34 if-converted vs HK$13.66)

Nickel Brazil acquisition (EU Phase II, long-stop ~Oct/Nov 2026): modelled as value-neutral; completion into an oversupplied nickel market is a modest negative, and the US$350m of June cash would leave the bridge
Related-party dependence on China Minmetals (offtake, logistics, financing) - a governance discount the DCF does not explicitly charge
Terminal multiple: 12x final-year FCF for a mine with reserves to ~2039; a reader using the Gordon value alone would add ~6% to base IV

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (intraday HK session); 52-week range HKD 6.21-11.96. FX from Yahoo HKD=X same day.
data_sources.financials: 1208.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, USD millions, FY2018-FY2025 + H1-2024/25/26); FY2025 Annual Report (segment tables, LME price table line 1461, capex plan line 3418, NCI subsidiary note line 11290, convertible note line 3888); H1-2026 Interim Report (gearing table line 1144, placing/convertibles line 1222, dilution table line 2093, NCI note 14 line 3913, LME price table line 364, Las Bambas segment line 548, subsequent events line 1568). Copper spot from Yahoo HG=F (COMEX, USD/lb).
data_sources.qualitative: 1208.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-16): guidance, Khoemacau expansion, Nickel Brazil EU review, August 2026 accident, analyst targets.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: ATTRIBUTABLE revenue, TTM to 30 June 2026 (FY2025 + H1-2026 - H1-2025). Consolidated TTM revenue 7,941.1 less NCI share: 37.5% x Las Bambas JV 5,748.1 (= 2,155.5) and 45% x Khoemacau JV 438.1 (= 197.1). Segment figures from FY2025 AR lines 1659/1990 and H1-2026 interim lines 548/3972.
inputs.share_count_basis: Issued shares at 30 June 2026 per the interim report's convertible-bond dilution table (line 2109), post the June 2026 placing. Held FLAT. The two zero-coupon convertibles (US$500m due Oct-2030 at HK$8.40 -> 463.1m shares; US$800m due Jun-2027 at HK$10.21 -> 613.9m shares) are carried as DEBT at face in net_debt and NOT added to the count; both are out of the money at the current price. If-converted treatment ((equity + US$1,300m) / (12,846m + 1,077m shares)) gives a LOWER per-share value only when IV exceeds ~HK$9.47, so debt treatment is the conservative one for every scenario except bull; the bull if-converted figure is noted in the narrative.
inputs.net_debt_basis: ATTRIBUTABLE, 30 June 2026. Consolidated: borrowings 2,566.4 + convertibles at FACE 1,300.0 (balance-sheet debt component 1,173.3) - cash 3,131.3 = 735.1. Less NCI share of JV-level net debt: 37.5% x (Las Bambas borrowings 1,210.0 - cash 1,481.4) = -101.8 and 45% x (Khoemacau borrowings 484.3 - cash 647.7) = -73.5, i.e. the NCI owns 175.3 of net cash, so attributable net debt = 735.1 + 175.3 = 910.4 (interim report lines 1144-1158). The US$274.3m Las Bambas dividend paid to NCI after period end (line 1572) does not change the attributable figure. Lease liabilities (131.0) EXCLUDED - see lease_treatment. The copper cash-flow hedge liability (24.0) is ignored as immaterial.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: reported_fcf is the ATTRIBUTABLE TTM owner-FCF estimate: consolidated TTM FCF 2,527.3 (OCF 3,738.4 - capex 1,211.1) less an estimated NCI share of ~710 (37.5% of Las Bambas EBITDA-less-tax-less-capex ~796, offset by 45% of Khoemacau's expansion-driven negative FCF ~-86). This is a PEAK-CYCLE figure (H1-2026 LME copper $13,088/t) and is NOT the projection base; the projections are built from components off base_revenue.
inputs.interest_income_note: TTM interest received 27.6 (consolidated) is NOT stripped: the group carries attributable NET DEBT, so cash is netted against debt in the bridge and interest income offsets excluded interest expense under the unlevered convention. No cash pile is being counted twice.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR cash-flow note line 11127-equivalent: share-based payment (1.3) FY2025, 3.1 FY2024, (1.5) FY2023 - immaterial, SBC-zero market; rows kept explicit at 0%
inputs.fx_note: USD -> HKD 7.8474, Yahoo Finance HKD=X on 2026-10-16. HKD is pegged to USD in a 7.75-7.85 band, so the rate is effectively fixed and no dual-listing parity check is needed; MMG has no second listing. All flows and per-share values are computed in USD and converted at this rate for the HKD quote-currency outputs.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Rf 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta 1.3 (copper miner) plus ~0.3% blended country-risk premium for Peru/DRC/Botswana -> cost of equity ~11%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (CDB/Minmetals term loans; the two convertibles are zero-coupon), ~3.7% after tax. Capital structure at market: equity ~US$12.5bn, debt ~US$3.9bn incl. convertibles at face -> 24% debt. WACC = 0.76 x 11% + 0.24 x 3.7% = 9.25%, rounded to 9.5%. Jurisdiction risk is charged HERE; commodity-price, blockade and operational risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights - not both. Same WACC in every scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost: full lease cash cost (principal ~36/yr + interest ~12/yr consolidated, FY2025 AR line 8501 and interim line 3208/3594; ~40/yr attributable) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.7% of attributable revenue. Lease liabilities (131.0 at 30 June 2026) EXCLUDED from net_debt. D&A paths are ex right-of-use depreciation in spirit (ROU depreciation is immaterial vs the 800+ mining D&A).
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows (proportional consolidation). NCI = 37.5% of Las Bambas JV Co. (Elion 22.5%, Citic Metal Peru 15%) and 45% of Khoemacau JV Co. (Comor). Every FY0 component (revenue, EBITDA, D&A, capex, net debt) has the NCI share stripped using the 100%-basis JV summaries in note 14 of the interim and note 'Principal Subsidiaries with Material NCI' of the FY2025 AR. There is NO NCI deduction in the bridge - charging both would double-count. Calibration: attributable TTM EBIT ~2,277 x (1-33%) = ~1,526 vs reported TTM attributable NPAT 1,066 (= 509.4 + 897.2 - 340.0); the gap is net finance cost ~250, Peru dividend WHT ~50 and the TTM accrual/cash tax difference, i.e. non-operating noise, so the leakage is calibrated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component engine), 10-year horizon, cyclical adaptations. MMG is an operating copper/zinc miner (Las Bambas Peru 62.5%, Khoemacau Botswana 55%, Kinsevere DRC, Dugald River and Rosebery Australia), 63.7% owned by China Minmetals; it is not a holdco, REIT or financial, so the owner-FCF engine applies with the section-7 adaptations: (1) currency - USD statements against an HKD quote, fx_rate recorded; (2) leases - treatment (B); (3) NCI - attributable flows; (4) SBC-zero - house and street coincide, band_position should be read as null; (5) risk charged once - jurisdiction in WACC, cycle/operations in scenarios. CYCLE POSITION: FY0 (TTM Jun-2026) sits at the top of the copper cycle - H1-2026 LME copper averaged $13,088/t, spot is ~$14,600/t (COMEX HG=F $6.62/lb on 2026-10-16), against $9,939/t in FY2025 and ~$9,100/t over FY2021-25. The base path therefore takes attributable revenue DOWN ~14% over years 2-3 to a $10,000/t copper / $3,500 gold / $45 silver / $2,900 zinc mid-cycle deck, then adds the Khoemacau expansion (130ktpa capacity, first production H1-2028, 55% attributable) in years 4-5. Mid-cycle EBITDA margin 50% (FY2025 attributable margin was 52% at $9,939 copper; FY2018-25 consolidated average 48%). CAPEX: FY2026 guided US$1,600-1,700m consolidated (Las Bambas 800-850, Khoemacau 500-550 incl. 400 expansion) -> ~1,105 attributable, then fading to a ~14.5%-of-revenue sustaining-plus-growth level once the expansion is built. CONVERTIBLES at face as debt, count flat (see share_count_basis). NICKEL BRAZIL (Anglo American, up to US$500m, EU Phase II review): not modelled - treated as value-neutral cash-for-assets at a fair price; if it completes, ~US$350m of the June cash leaves for ferronickel assets in a currently oversupplied market, which would be a modest negative to revisit. FY0 fully-diluted count is the 30-June basic count because the only dilutive instruments are the convertibles, carried as debt. Buybacks: none ever; dividends: none since 2012 (dividend policy adopted FY2025, nothing declared) - the flat count is a convention the company has not had to fund, but with SBC at zero there is nothing to fund.

bear.rationale: Copper reverts hard to $8,500/t by Y3 (a China/global slowdown deck, roughly the FY2022-24 average), gold/silver give back half their 2025-26 gain, and a Las Bambas corridor blockade year lands in Y2 (the asset has lost ~600 days to stoppages since 2016; Peru's 2026 election cycle and the August 2026 fatal accident are the live triggers). Margins settle at 42% (FY2022-24 consolidated average was ~42%). Khoemacau ramps a year late. Peru tax/royalty regime tightens (35% cash rate). Expansion capex overruns. Terminal cap 10x on a shorter effective mine life. Same WACC.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 (12m to Jun-27): copper averages ~$12,000/t (partial reversion from $14,600 spot), volumes +3% (FY2026 guidance up to 528kt Cu, 235kt Zn) -> +2%. Y2-Y3: deck normalises to $10,000/t copper, $3,500 gold, $45 silver, $2,900 zinc -> -8%, -6%. Y4-Y5: Khoemacau expansion first concentrate H1-2028, ramping to 130ktpa (55% attributable, ~+11% attributable copper volume) -> +5%, +5%. Y6-10: flat volumes, 2% price drift. 10-yr CAGR 0.7%.
base.margin_rationale: TTM attributable 55.4% at peak prices; FY2025 attributable 52.1% at $9,939 copper. Mid-cycle 50% reflects the deck above net of Peru profit-share incentives and cost inflation. Las Bambas C1 guidance $0.85-1.05/lb is flattered by by-product credits that normalise with gold/silver.
base.capex_rationale: Y1-Y2 at the FY2026 guided US$1.6-1.7bn consolidated (~1,105 attributable, 19.5%) while the Khoemacau US$400m/yr expansion and Las Bambas Ferrobamba/tailings works run; Y3 steps down as the expansion completes; Y4+ 14.5% (~800 attributable) covers sustaining capital plus the stated growth pipeline (Khoemacau phase 2 to 200kt, Ferrobamba Deeps, bolt-ons).
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax on EBIT at 33%: Peru 29.5% corporate + 8% workers' participation at Las Bambas (~35% effective), Australia 30%, DRC 30%, Botswana 22%, plus Peru 5% dividend WHT on repatriation. TTM cash tax paid 960 vs accrual 1,118 on consolidated EBIT 3,407; attributable accrual ~32%. No interest shield taken (unlevered).
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 12x final-year FCF binds against Gordon (12.7x at 9.5%/1.5%): Las Bambas reserves support operations to ~2039 (plus Ferrobamba Deeps/Sulfobamba extension potential), Dugald River into the 2030s; a finite-life, mid-curve copper producer does not earn a perpetual-growth multiple.

bull.rationale: The structural-deficit copper thesis holds: copper averages $13,000/t in Y1 and settles at $12,000/t rather than $10,000/t, gold/silver stay elevated, Las Bambas delivers the top of the 380-400kt range every year with no corridor stoppages, Khoemacau ramps to 130kt on schedule and phase 2 (200kt) is sanctioned. Margins hold at the current 55%; capex falls faster post-expansion. Same WACC; terminal cap 13x. If-converted check: at this scenario's IV both convertibles are in the money, and the if-converted per-share value ((equity + US$1,300m) / 13,923m shares) is ~2.3% lower than the debt-treatment figure shown (HK$13.34 vs HK$13.66) - the bull number is modestly overstated on that basis.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: single-asset (Las Bambas) and single-corridor concentration with a documented ~600 days of stoppages since 2016, a live Peru election cycle and fatal-accident investigation, three higher-sovereign-risk host countries, and a controlling shareholder whose related-party offtake and financing sit on both sides of the P&L. The base case already charges the price normalisation, so the bear is about operational disruption and a deeper price trough on top. Bull trimmed to 20% because it needs the current peak price regime to persist for a decade AND flawless execution at two JV mines - a conjunction, not one thing going right. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
